discovery: Development of matter-wave (atom) interferometry for precision measurement

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Université Paris 13 / SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris

subfield: Atomic physics / quantum sensing and precision measurement
motivation: Atom interferometry turned the wave nature of matter into one of physics' most precise measuring instruments. Bordé showed that atomic transitions driven by light act as beam splitters, providing the theoretical foundation; Pritchard's group built the first atom interferometer with nanofabricated gratings (1991) and pioneered its use for fundamental measurements; Kasevich (with Chu) realized light-pulse atom interferometry the same year and developed it into ultra-precise gravimeters, gyroscopes and gradiometers. These instruments now yield the most precise determinations of the fine-structure constant, testing QED and the Standard Model at the parts-per-trillion level, measure Newton's constant, test the equivalence principle with quantum objects, and underpin a new generation of experiments searching for ultralight dark matter and mid-band gravitational waves, such as MAGIS-100 and AION. This is a rare case in which quantum-mechanical insight and heroic instrumentation together opened an entirely new window on fundamental physics.
